Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An illuminator apparatus and method for illuminating an object field imaged by a rectangular image sensor having a first aspect ratio is disclosed. The apparatus includes an optical fiber having a proximal end disposed to receive a plurality of input light beams, each light beam having differing spectral properties, the optical fiber being operable to transmit the light beams along the fiber to a distal end of the optical fiber. The apparatus also includes an integrating element disposed to receive the light beams from the distal end of the fiber and combine the light beams to produce a generally homogenous illumination beam at a rectangular output face of the integrating element. The apparatus further includes an illumination projector operable to project an image of the output face of the integrating element into the object field to produce a generally rectangular illuminated region of the object field substantially corresponding to the portion of the object field imaged by the rectangular image sensor.

outputs.L1:
Disclosed is an illuminator apparatus and method for illuminating an object field imaged by a rectangular image sensor having a first aspect ratio. The apparatus includes an optical fiber with a proximal end positioned to receive a plurality of input light beams, each having different spectral properties. The optical fiber is configured to transmit the light beams along the fiber to a distal end thereof.

The apparatus further includes an integrating element positioned to receive the light beams from the distal end of the optical fiber and to combine the light beams, thereby producing a generally homogeneous illumination beam at a rectangular output face of the integrating element.

The apparatus also includes an illumination projector configured to project an image of the output face of the integrating element into the object field, producing a generally rectangular illuminated region of the object field that substantially corresponds to the portion of the object field imaged by the rectangular image sensor.
outputs.L2: Disclosed is an illumination device and associated technique for lighting an object field that is captured by a rectangular image sensor with a first aspect ratio. The device has an optical fiber with a proximal end positioned to accept multiple incoming light beams, where the beams have different spectral characteristics. The optical fiber is configured to carry these light beams through the fiber to its distal end. An integrating component is arranged to receive the beams emitted from the fiber’s distal end and merge them, forming a substantially uniform illumination beam at a rectangular exit face of the integrating component. The device also includes an illumination projector configured to project an image of that exit face into the object field, thereby creating a generally rectangular illuminated area that substantially matches the part of the object field imaged by the rectangular image sensor.
outputs.L3:
The apparatus is configured to illuminate an object field that is imaged by a rectangular image sensor having a first aspect ratio. In operation, the image sensor captures a corresponding rectangular portion of the object field, and the illumination system is arranged so that the illuminated area substantially matches this imaged portion.

The apparatus includes an optical fiber that receives a plurality of input light beams. These input light beams may differ from one another in their spectral properties, such as wavelength range, color, bandwidth, or spectral distribution. The optical fiber transmits the received light beams toward its distal end, where the beams are delivered to an integrating element.

The integrating element receives the transmitted light beams and combines them to form a generally homogeneous illumination beam. By mixing the different input beams, the integrating element reduces spatial non-uniformities and produces a more even distribution of light. The integrating element includes a rectangular output face from which the combined illumination beam exits.

An illumination projector is positioned to image the rectangular output face of the integrating element into the object field. In this way, the shape and aspect ratio of the integrating element’s output face are transferred, or substantially transferred, to the illuminated region within the object field.

As a result, the projected illumination forms a generally rectangular illuminated region in the object field. This illuminated region corresponds to the portion of the object field that is imaged by the rectangular image sensor, thereby providing efficient and uniform illumination over the area captured by the sensor.
outputs.L4:
An illuminator apparatus and associated method are provided for producing illumination that is closely matched to the field of view of a rectangular image sensor. The apparatus includes one or more radiation sources configured to generate a plurality of input beams having different spectral characteristics, such as different wavelengths, wavelength bands, or colors. The input beams may be supplied by separate light-emitting diodes, laser diodes, filtered lamps, or other suitable optical sources. These beams are coupled into an optical fiber or fiber bundle so that the spectrally different components are delivered along a common optical path.

At an output end of the optical fiber, the light is directed into an integrating or homogenizing element. The integrating element may be formed as a light pipe, mixing rod, integrator bar, or similar optical component having reflective internal surfaces that promote multiple reflections of the transmitted light. Through these reflections, spatial variations among the input beams are reduced, and the spectral components are mixed to form a more uniform output distribution. The integrating element preferably has an output face that is rectangular, or otherwise shaped to correspond to the aspect ratio of the image sensor.

Projection optics are arranged to image the rectangular output face of the integrating element into an object field to be viewed by the imaging system. The projected illumination forms a generally homogeneous rectangular illuminated region at the object plane. The size, shape, and aspect ratio of this illuminated region are selected to substantially correspond to the area imaged by the rectangular sensor. As a result, light is concentrated primarily within the useful imaging field rather than being spread over areas outside the sensor’s field of view.

In operation, the spectrally different input beams are generated, coupled into the optical fiber, transmitted to the integrating element, and homogenized. The homogenized light exiting the rectangular output face is then projected onto the object field. The object field is simultaneously or subsequently imaged by the rectangular image sensor. Because the illuminated region is matched to the sensor-imaged region, the system provides improved illumination efficiency, reduced wasted light, and more uniform exposure across the captured image.

The disclosed illuminator may be used in machine vision, medical imaging, microscopy, inspection systems, endoscopy, spectroscopy, or any application in which a rectangular detector or camera sensor benefits from illumination having a corresponding rectangular shape. By combining spectral mixing, fiber delivery, optical homogenization, and rectangular field projection, the apparatus provides a compact and efficient way to generate uniform illumination that is well aligned with the geometry of the imaging sensor.
outputs.L5:
**The**

“The” is one of the smallest words in English, but it is also one of the most important. It is called the definite article, and it is used when we are talking about something specific or already known. For example, in the sentence “I saw the dog,” the word “the” tells us that the speaker and listener know which dog is being discussed.

Unlike many other English words, “the” does not have a strong meaning on its own. Instead, it helps give meaning to the words around it. It can point to a particular person, place, thing, or idea: “the sun,” “the city,” “the answer,” or “the best choice.” It can also make a noun feel unique or important.

The word “the” appears everywhere in English. It is used in books, conversations, songs, news reports, and everyday speech. Even though it is short and simple, it helps sentences become clearer and more precise. Without “the,” English would sound much less natural.

In many ways, “the” shows how powerful small words can be. It may not attract much attention, but it plays a key role in communication. It helps us understand exactly what is being talked about and connects ideas smoothly in a sentence.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an illumination system that combines multiple spectral light beams through an optical fiber and integrating element to illuminate a rectangular camera sensor field.
counterfactuals.output: An illumination system includes a plurality of light sources configured to generate respective spectral light beams of different wavelength ranges. The spectral light beams are combined and coupled into an optical fiber, which delivers the combined light to an integrating element. The integrating element homogenizes the combined light and outputs a substantially uniform illumination beam. Projection optics are arranged to shape and direct the illumination beam onto a rectangular field corresponding to an active area of a camera sensor. The system thereby provides spectrally selectable or spectrally combined, spatially uniform illumination over the rectangular sensor field, with improved coupling efficiency and reduced non-uniformity among the different spectral components.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a single-paragraph patent disclosure describing an apparatus and method for producing homogeneous rectangular illumination matched to a rectangular image sensor.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus and method are disclosed for producing substantially homogeneous rectangular illumination matched to a rectangular image sensor, the apparatus comprising a light source, such as one or more LEDs, laser diodes, or broadband emitters, an optical mixing element configured to spatially homogenize light emitted by the light source, and a rectangular beam-shaping optical system arranged to transform the homogenized light into an illumination field having an aspect ratio and active area corresponding to the aspect ratio and photosensitive area of the rectangular image sensor. In one embodiment, the optical mixing element comprises an integrating rod, light pipe, diffuser, microlens array, or compound parabolic concentrator having a rectangular output aperture, and the beam-shaping optical system comprises one or more refractive, reflective, diffractive, or freeform optical elements that image or project the rectangular output aperture onto an object plane, sensor plane, intermediate plane, or field of view observed by the rectangular image sensor. The apparatus may further include an aperture stop, field stop, mask, telecentric relay, condenser lens, cylindrical lens, anamorphic lens group, or freeform lens surface selected to control edge sharpness, angular distribution, numerical aperture, and illumination uniformity across the rectangular field. The dimensions of the rectangular illumination region are selected to coincide with, slightly exceed, or be optically conjugate to the active pixel region of the image sensor, thereby reducing wasted optical power outside the sensed field and improving signal-to-noise ratio, exposure uniformity, and thermal efficiency. The method comprises emitting light from the light source, coupling the light into the optical mixing element to reduce spatial nonuniformity, shaping the mixed light into a rectangular distribution having predetermined length and width dimensions, and directing the shaped distribution onto a target or directly onto the sensor field such that the illuminated region is registered with the rectangular imaging area. In some embodiments, a controller adjusts source intensity, relative source drive currents, movable apertures, adaptive optical elements, or sensor feedback to maintain a selected irradiance profile, including a flat-top rectangular profile, a controlled roll-off profile near the edges, or a profile compensated for lens vignetting or sensor sensitivity variation. The apparatus and method thereby provide efficient, uniform, rectangular illumination for machine vision, microscopy, document imaging, biometric imaging, medical imaging, or other imaging systems employing rectangular image sensors.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent claim-like summary for an illuminator using an optical fiber, an integrating rod with a rectangular output face, and a projection lens to illuminate an object field.
counterfactuals.output:
An illuminator comprising:

an optical fiber configured to deliver illumination light from a light source;

an integrating rod optically coupled to an output end of the optical fiber, the integrating rod being configured to receive the illumination light and homogenize the illumination light by internal reflection, the integrating rod having a rectangular output face defining a rectangular illumination aperture; and

a projection lens disposed downstream of the rectangular output face and configured to image the rectangular output face onto an object field,

wherein the rectangular output face and the projection lens cooperate to produce a substantially uniform rectangular illumination field at the object field.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, an imaging illumination apparatus where different colored input beams are mixed and projected as a uniform rectangular region corresponding to the sensor’s field of view.
counterfactuals.output:
An imaging illumination apparatus comprises an illumination source assembly, an optical mixing assembly, and a projection assembly disposed along an optical path. The illumination source assembly is configured to generate a plurality of input light beams having respectively different spectral characteristics, including at least a first input light beam of a first color and a second input light beam of a second color different from the first color. The plurality of input light beams are directed toward the optical mixing assembly.

The optical mixing assembly is configured to receive and spatially combine the plurality of input light beams to form a composite illumination beam. In one embodiment, the optical mixing assembly includes one or more beam-combining elements, such as dichroic mirrors, prisms, light guides, integrators, homogenizers, diffusers, or lens arrays, arranged to superimpose the different colored input beams and to reduce spatial non-uniformity of the combined light. The optical mixing assembly thereby produces a mixed output beam having a substantially uniform color distribution and a substantially uniform irradiance profile over a predetermined cross-sectional region.

The projection assembly is optically coupled to the optical mixing assembly and is configured to project the mixed output beam onto a target region. The projection assembly shapes the mixed output beam into a substantially rectangular illumination region corresponding to, or substantially coextensive with, a field of view of an image sensor of an imaging device. The rectangular illumination region may be dimensioned to match an active sensing area, aspect ratio, or projected field of view of the image sensor, such that substantially all portions of the sensor field of view receive substantially uniform illumination.

In operation, light of different colors emitted by the illumination source assembly is combined by the optical mixing assembly to form a spectrally mixed illumination beam. The beam is homogenized and shaped by the projection assembly so that, at an object plane associated with the image sensor field of view, the illumination defines a uniform rectangular area. The apparatus thereby provides controlled, multi-color, spatially uniform illumination for image acquisition over the region observed by the sensor.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for an invention involving fiber-delivered multi-spectral light, an integrating element, and an illumination projector for rectangular field illumination.
counterfactuals.output: An illumination system includes a multi-spectral light source coupled to one or more optical fibers for delivering light of different wavelengths to a projection assembly. The projection assembly includes an integrating element positioned to receive the fiber-delivered multi-spectral light and to spatially homogenize and combine the received light into a substantially uniform output beam. An illumination projector optically coupled to the integrating element shapes and directs the homogenized light onto a target area as a rectangular illumination field. The integrating element may comprise a light pipe, integrating rod, mixing chamber, or other homogenizing optic, and the projector may include one or more lenses, apertures, or beam-shaping optics configured to control the size, aspect ratio, and uniformity of the rectangular field. The system provides compact, remotely sourceable, multi-wavelength illumination with improved spectral mixing and spatial uniformity for applications including imaging, inspection, sensing, medical illumination, and machine vision.
